narrative.overview: The globe is the observed object; every piece of chrome is a calibrated instrument pointed at it. The map fills the viewport edge to edge, floating in a space-dark surround that never changes with the theme — what changes is the instrument housing around it: warm sand fittings in light mode, charcoal-and-starlight in dark. Panels, HUDs, and cards are frosted glass lenses hovering over the world, never walls beside it; when a panel opens, the camera shifts the planet, not the layout. The mood is precise, quiet, luminous. Exactly two accents exist and each has one meaning: ice is how you find your way, signal is the live pulse of play. The chrome never raises its voice — the fun lives in the copy and the game feedback, not in the hue system.
keyCharacteristics: Map-first, full-bleed globe; all UI floats above it at fixed positions
Two semantic accents (ice / signal) with hard-assigned meanings; everything else colored is a data encoding, not an accent
Frosted-glass surface language: translucent cards + backdrop blur over the living map
Instrument typography: Outfit for display/body, system mono + tabular-nums for every number that matters
Space-dark backdrop in both themes; light/dark only re-skins the instrument housing
WCAG AA enforced by construction: every accent has a documented accessible variant per surface

rules.name: The Two-Accent Rule
rules.body: Ice means interactive/wayfinding; signal means live game state/loss. No third accent exists, and neither accent ever borrows the other's meaning. Anything else with hue is a data encoding and must be justifiable as one.

rules.name: The Accessible-Pair Rule
rules.body: Light surfaces carry the deep variants for text (text-ice-accessible dark:text-ice, text-signal-accessible dark:text-signal); dark surfaces carry the bare accents. Never place bare ice or signal text on a sand surface.

rules.name: The Retirement Rule
rules.body: Teal (#14b8a6 family) and coral (#f43f5e family) are retired and pinned absent by designTokens.test.ts. Do not reintroduce them under any name.

rules.name: The Colorless-Role Rule
rules.body: The three type-role utilities (.text-readout, .text-display, .text-label) carry no color; color is always applied per-usage via the accessible-pair pattern.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number a player might watch change renders in tabular numerals — .text-readout where the mono voice fits, tabular-nums at minimum.

rules.name: The Frosted Card Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one floating-surface recipe: bg-sand-50/95 dark:bg-dark-400/95 + backdrop-blur-xl + rounded-2xl + hairline border. Do not invent a second card material.

rules.name: The Space-Dark Rule
rules.body: The page backdrop stays space-dark in both themes. Themes re-skin the instruments, never the sky.

dos: Do write every interactive text color as the pair text-ice-accessible dark:text-ice (and signal text as text-signal-accessible dark:text-signal).
Do reuse the Frosted Card Rule recipe for any new floating surface, and the ice-family focus-visible:ring-2 for any new control.
Do keep entrances in the house motion grammar: 100-300ms ease-out fade + 6-12px rise, 50-60ms staggers; expose data-animation-state on any component that animates, and respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Do grow sub-44px controls to the 44px floor with the TOUCH_TARGET_* invisible-inset pattern — never by inflating glyphs.
Do update src/lib/layoutConstants.ts (and its pin test) when changing panel geometry, and expect designTokens.test.ts to fail if a pinned token hex or type-role declaration drifts.
donts: Don't introduce a third accent, use signal for anything interactive, or use ice for game-state feedback.
Don't reintroduce retired hexes: teal #14b8a6/#5eead4/#0d9488, coral #f43f5e/#fb7185/#e11d48, or the old amber reveal #f59e0b.
Don't place bare ice (#7dd3fc) or signal (#ff8a4c) text on sand surfaces — both fail AA there; the accessible variants exist for exactly this.
Don't create a second card material, a second focus treatment, or a second primary-button recipe.
Don't theme the page backdrop — space-dark in both themes is a settled owner decision.
